_note: The UI PHYSICS corpus (ui-motion.md phase 2) — three pure folds the native UI elements call instead of each re-deriving their own feel. THE DECAY / FLING LAW is the UIScrollView deceleration model in its CONTINUOUS form: with the deceleration rate d = 0.998 per millisecond (UIScrollView.DecelerationRate.normal) the time constant is τ = −1 / ln(d) ms ≈ 499.4998 ms, position is x(t) = x0 + v0·τ·(1 − e^(−t/τ)) with v0 in points per MILLISECOND, the RESTING offset is the limit x0 + v0·τ, and the clip ends when |v| falls under the terminal threshold 0.001 pt/ms (1 pt/s) at t = τ·ln(|v0| / 0.001) — a fling released at or under the threshold does NOT MOVE AT ALL (x(t) = x0 for every t, target = x0) and lasts 0 ms, never a negative duration. THE RUBBER-BAND LAW is the standard iOS overscroll compression f(x) = (1 − 1 / (|x|·c/d + 1))·d · sign(x) with c = 0.55 and d the dimension being overscrolled — asymptotic: no finger travel ever moves the content more than d past the edge. `rubberBandInverse` is its exact inverse (x = (d/c)·(1/(1 − |y|/d) − 1), |y| clamped just inside d) so a gesture can be resumed from a compressed offset — each case's `inverse` is the ROUND TRIP rubberBandInverse(rubberBand(x, d), d), fed the runner's own unrounded y, and it must return x. A zero/negative dimension yields 0 (no travel) on both. THE RELEASE spring is the pinned constant RUBBER_BAND_RELEASE = spring(response 0.35 s, dampingFraction 1.0) — critically damped, because an overscroll snapping back must never bounce past the edge it is returning to. THE SNAP LAW: project the release with the decay fold, then take the NEAREST snap point to that projection; an exact tie takes the LOWER point (deterministic on all three runtimes). This is the one law behind sheet detents, pagers and pickers. Offsets and dimensions are in POINTS, velocities in points per millisecond; all floats 6 decimals, tolerance 1.5e-6; independent scratch derivation.

decay.name: a rightward fling from 0 at 2 pt/ms
a slow drag release below the terminal threshold never moves
zero velocity rests where it was released

rubberBand.name: a small overscroll is nearly linear
a full-dimension overscroll compresses to about a third
compression is asymptotic — 10x the dimension still fits inside it
a zero dimension yields no travel

snap.name: a released sheet with no velocity snaps to the nearest detent
a flick projects past the nearest detent
a hard flick projects to the far detent
a downward flick returns to the closed detent
a projection past the last point clamps to it
an exact tie takes the LOWER point
